name: DoorDash
thesis: DoorDash is the strongest US local-commerce demand network, with order density, DashPass, advertising, and category expansion supporting durable growth. The operating thesis is credible, but the security remains on the evaluation list rather than approved for new money because the price embeds too much of the upside. The revised DCF is about $122 base, $194 bull, and $43 bear versus a recent market price around $196. The base assumes 18% near-term revenue growth fading to 4%, a 19.5% terminal operating margin, and 14x exit. A purchase requires either a materially lower price or evidence that Deliveroo/Wolt integration, non-restaurant growth, and advertising can lift margin without slowing order growth or cash conversion.
key_driver: Marketplace GOV growth x net revenue margin x contribution margin, constrained by acquisition integration and reinvestment

tier_1_kpis.break_condition: Negative YoY for 2 consecutive quarters while organic GOV growth is below 20%

thesis_breakers_qualitative: Organic order growth falls below low teens for two quarters
Adjusted EBITDA / GOV remains below 2% despite slowing reinvestment
Deliveroo or Wolt integration requires sustained capital without clear contribution-profit improvement
Advertising or take-rate gains provoke merchant churn or lower order frequency
Free cash flow declines while acquisition-adjusted revenue growth slows below 15%

break_rules.narrative: Revenue declining YoY for 2 consecutive quarters.
FCF margin below 5% for 2 consecutive quarters.

bear_deltas.note: Owner approved 2026-07-29. The simplified thesis seed captures slower organic order growth, acquisition-integration drag, and weaker delivery economics. The live workbook uses -6pp/-3pp near/terminal growth and -4pp/-7pp near/terminal margin, producing about $43 per share.

segments.name: Total company
segments.description: US and international local-commerce marketplace, including restaurant, grocery, retail, advertising, Wolt, and Deliveroo.

business_model_rules.narrative: Organic order growth below 12% for 2 quarters means density and frequency are no longer supporting the modeled growth path.
Adjusted EBITDA / GOV below 2% for 2 quarters indicates reinvestment or competition is overwhelming scale economics.
Free cash flow declining for 2 quarters while organic growth slows is incompatible with the terminal-margin thesis.
